holidays.name: National Margarita Day
holidays.description: A salt-rimmed celebration of the tequila, lime, and orange liqueur cocktail that has fueled patio gatherings and Tex-Mex dinners for decades. Bars and restaurants often roll out specials, and home bartenders break out their blenders.
holidays.origin: An unofficial food and drink holiday that grew out of American cocktail culture and is widely promoted by bars, restaurants, and liquor brands. The exact founder is unclear, and it is not a government-recognized observance.
holidays.funFact: The margarita's origin is hotly disputed. Claimants include a Tijuana restaurateur, a Dallas socialite, and a Galveston bartender, all supposedly from the 1930s and 1940s, and all of them say they invented it.

holidays.name: Walking the Dog Day
holidays.description: A day dedicated to leashing up your four-legged friend and heading outside for a good stroll. It celebrates the bond between people and pups and encourages exercise for both ends of the leash.
holidays.origin: An unofficial pet-themed observance created by pet enthusiasts and promoted in the lists of quirky holidays. It has no single documented founder.
holidays.funFact: Studies have found that dog owners tend to walk more than people without dogs, often by several hours per week. So the dog is technically walking you.

holidays.name: Be Humble Day
holidays.description: A day to quietly reflect, skip the bragging, and give credit to others. The irony of announcing your humility on a holiday is part of the fun.
holidays.origin: An unofficial awareness observance that appears in quirky holiday calendars. It promotes modesty and gratitude, and its creator is not well documented.
holidays.funFact: The word humble comes from the Latin humilis, meaning low or on the ground, which is itself derived from humus, the Latin word for earth.

holidays.name: Cook a Sweet Potato Day
holidays.description: A day for baking, roasting, mashing, or frying the humble orange root vegetable. Sweet potatoes are celebrated for their flavor, versatility, and fiber content.
holidays.origin: A food-focused unofficial observance popular among food bloggers and home cooks. It is part of the long calendar of produce-themed days.
holidays.funFact: Sweet potatoes are not closely related to regular potatoes. They belong to the morning glory family, while regular potatoes are in the nightshade family.

holidays.name: Thinking Day
holidays.description: A global day when Girl Guides and Girl Scouts around the world think about each other, celebrate international friendship, and often raise funds for community causes.
holidays.origin: Established in 1926 at a Girl Guide and Girl Scout conference in the USA. February 22 was chosen because it is the shared birthday of Scouting founder Robert Baden-Powell and his wife Olave, who was World Chief Guide.
holidays.funFact: Since 1926 the day has been observed by millions of members in over 150 countries. It was originally called Thinking Day, but is now also known as World Thinking Day.
